posts.label: Intro carousel — pin to top of grid
posts.caption:
Hello 👋

This is CasuallyGenerous: a collection of small, mostly free, generous things to do with people you're already spending time with — friends, family, a partner, colleagues.

Not volunteering. Not donations. The bit in between.

Every idea is sorted by effort: Spontaneous (do it today), Planned (needs a date in the diary), Committed (sign up once, then it's yours).

Built by one person, for fun, no ads. Browse them all at the link in bio.

Did one? Tag #CasuallyGenerous — we'll share it.

posts.label: Invite a neighbour who lives alone to dinner
posts.hook: Cooking for four? Make it five.
steps: Next time you're having people round, think of the neighbour you nod at but never really talk to.
Knock and ask a few days ahead. A note through the door works too.
Keep it a normal dinner, not a rescue mission. Same food, same chat.
If it goes well, there's a standing extra seat from now on.
posts.why: Plenty of people eat alone most nights. An invitation costs you one plate, and can give someone an evening they'll still be thinking about next week.
posts.caption:
You're having people round anyway. Lay one more place.

The neighbour who lives on their own probably eats alone most nights — and a knock on the door with a dinner invite is about the easiest generous thing there is.

Swipe for how to ask without it being awkward. Full how-to at the link in bio.

Who's the neighbour you'd ask? Send this to whoever you're cooking with.

posts.label: Refill empty Halloween sweet bowls
posts.caption:
Halloween this Saturday. Small idea for whoever's doing the rounds with kids:

Carry a spare bag of sweets and top up the empty bowls on doorsteps as you go — so the last trick-or-treaters of the night don't walk away with nothing.

Costs a couple of quid. Link in bio for more like this.

posts.label: Instead of the pub → teach each other a skill
posts.y: Teach each other a new skill
posts.note: One of you teaches the rest something you're genuinely good at — knitting, chess, investing, whatever. Rotate who hosts.
posts.caption:
Nothing against the pub. But every so often, swap it for this:

One person teaches everyone else something they're properly good at. Bread, chess, budgeting, a card trick. Next time someone else hosts.

You learn something, and the person teaching gets to be good at something out loud. Link in bio.

What would you teach? 👇

posts.label: Clean up trash in a local park
posts.hook: Your next park catch-up, with bin bags.
steps: Pick your usual park and message whoever you'd meet there anyway.
Bring gloves and a few bin bags — a litter picker if anyone has one.
Set a 60-minute timer and split up the area.
Bag it, leave it by a park bin, then go and get tacos.
posts.why: Litter tends to attract more litter, so a cleaner patch is less likely to get dumped on. And you get an hour of easy company with something to show for it.
posts.caption:
Same park. Same people. One hour. A few bin bags.

Then tacos — that part's not optional.

Swipe for the 4-step version, and send this to the friend you'd drag along. Full how-to at the link in bio.

posts.label: Clear a neighbour's path or garden
posts.caption:
Leaf season. If you're already out there with the rake, do next door's bit too.

Ten more minutes for you. For a neighbour who struggles with it, one less thing to worry about.

More small ones like this at the link in bio.

posts.label: Roundup: three things for a cold weekend
posts.title: Three small things for a cold weekend
posts.caption:
Cold weekend plans, one for every level of effort:

🩷 Spontaneous — write cards to people who won't expect one
💙 Planned — run a clothes and style exchange
💚 Committed — book a first aid course together

Pick one. All three are at the link in bio.

Send this to whoever you're spending the weekend with.

posts.label: Write an appreciation email to an old teacher
posts.hook: Which teacher changed something for you?
steps: Over a drink, each of you names the teacher who mattered — and why.
Find their school's contact email. Most schools will pass a message on.
Write three sentences: what they did, what it changed, thank you.
Hit send together, before anyone overthinks it.
posts.why: Most teachers rarely find out how things turned out for their students. A short, specific thank-you tends to land far harder than the fifteen minutes it takes to write.
posts.caption:
Most teachers never find out.

The one who noticed you, pushed you, or just made a subject click — they probably have no idea.

Swipe for how to do it in 15 minutes with friends. Link in bio.

Who's yours? Tag a friend who'd know theirs.

posts.label: Leave real comments for small online creators
posts.caption:
Find someone making something good for an audience of forty people. Tell them specifically what you liked.

Not a 🔥. An actual sentence.

For a small creator, one thoughtful comment can be the reason they post again next week. Link in bio for more.

posts.label: World Kindness Day roundup
posts.title: Three ways to mark it with someone
posts.caption:
It's World Kindness Day. Three ways to mark it, from five minutes to a weekend:

🩷 Email a company to praise one of their staff — compliments almost never get sent
💙 Throw a thank-you party for someone who's never been properly thanked
💚 Book a mental health first aid course together

All at the link in bio. Which one are you doing?

posts.label: Do a home energy audit together
posts.hook: Where is your heating actually going?
steps: Pick a cold, windy afternoon and get a friend round.
Go room by room with the back of a damp hand — you'll feel the draughts.
Note gaps around doors, windows, letterboxes and the loft hatch.
Next weekend, swap houses and do theirs.
posts.why: Draughts are among the cheapest things to fix in a home and among the most noticeable on a cold day. Fewer leaks generally means lower bills and less energy used.
posts.caption:
Heating on, still cold? An afternoon with a friend finds most of the reason.

Room by room, hunting draughts. Then swap and do their place next weekend.

Swipe for the 4 steps. Full how-to (and the cheap fixes) at the link in bio.

posts.label: Write reviews for local independent businesses
posts.caption:
That café you keep going back to? Half an hour and your phone.

For a small independent, a handful of honest reviews can change who finds them. Do it over the coffee itself.

Link in bio for more small ones.

posts.label: Instead of a takeaway → farmers market + cook
posts.y: Shop at a farmers market and cook together
posts.note: Buy dinner from the people who grew it, then cook it together. Better food, actual conversation.
posts.caption:
Saturday swap: skip the takeaway.

Go to the market together, buy dinner from whoever grew it, and cook it that evening. You'll talk more in the kitchen than you would over a delivery bag.

Link in bio. Who are you cooking with tonight?
